# bdwgc: repairing a garbage collector without a test suite

The repository has received 27 separate undocumented edits.

This project is a library that hands out storage to a running program and later takes back whatever that program can no longer reach, along with a facility for building up long pieces of text out of smaller fragments. Both sides of it now misbehave. Simple programs abort before they do any work, longer-running ones crash or quietly hand the same storage to two owners at once, and several ordinary calls refuse requests they used to serve.

The trouble starts with the simplest thing a program can ask for. Requesting one small block and doing nothing else aborts inside that call, with the library reporting that one of its own internal consistency checks failed. Building it in the mode that keeps extra bookkeeping beside every object, and allocating through the entry points that go with that mode, aborts too, on a different internal check, this one raised for ordinary small requests. Asking for a block of zero bytes aborts rather than coming back with memory. Handing an object back explicitly and then asking for a fresh block of the same size yields storage that still holds the bytes written into the object just given up, rather than zeros. Passing a null pointer to the call that gives an object back crashes instead of returning without doing anything.
